description: 🔴 **BLOCKING DEFECT — the 'general trainer' has no training engine, and lugh's refusal grammar routes to it.** Verified 2026-08-11: `trainer/src` contains **zero imports** of `torch`, `transformers`, `trl`, `peft`, `accelerate` — or even `subprocess`. Its complete third-party set is `fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic, httpx, jsonschema, referencing`. `llama_factory.py:145` falls back to `recorded_text_run()` — a JSON fixture — and the docstring's 'shells out to LLaMA-Factory' path **does not exist in code**. Meanwhile ROADMAP lists KFT as *'`trainer/` **general** provider implemented & gated'*, and **D9 makes this the documented destination for every job lugh refuses**: lugh's graded refusal codes name agora's general trainer as where an out-of-envelope job should go. So the refusal-routing contract currently routes to a fixture replayer. **Either outcome is acceptable; the current state is not.** Note `50-finetune-live-endpoints` does NOT cover this — it stands up the §6/§5.3/§8 *endpoints*, which is the contract surface, not the engine behind it.

userStories.title: Decide, and record, which agora is building
userStories.description: Two legitimate answers. Pick one in writing before any code moves.
acceptanceCriteria: An ADR records either **(a) adopt a real engine** — LLaMA-Factory (73,993★ Apache-2.0) or Axolotl (12,339★ Apache-2.0) behind the existing `run_source` seam, which is already the injection point — or **(b) agora does not train**, and the general-trainer role is retired or re-scoped.
The decision confronts the real cost of (a): agora inherits torch and a GPU story it deliberately does not have today, which is presumably why the fixture design exists in the first place.
If (b), the ADR states what happens to D9 — lugh's refusal codes must name a destination that exists, so either another provider takes the role or the refusal grammar changes.
Whichever way it lands, the frozen conformance corpus and the KFT contract surface are unaffected — this is about the engine, not the wire.
userStories.notes: The fixture-replay design is HONEST in its docstring. The failure is that nothing above it says so, and a contract in another repo points here.

userStories.title: Stop reporting a capability that is not there
userStories.description: Independent of US-1, and cheap. This is the minimum fix even if the engine question stays open.
acceptanceCriteria: `POST /invoke` returns a **graded refusal** rather than replaying a fixture when no engine is configured — a provider that cannot train must say so in the KFT vocabulary, which is exactly the discipline lugh is praised for.
README and ROADMAP stop describing the general trainer as implemented; the honest state is stated with what would change it.

A test asserts that with no engine configured, `invoke` refuses rather than returning a plausible-looking recorded run — a fixture that reads as a completed training run is the worst failure shape here, because a caller cannot tell it apart from success.

The KCB manifest stops advertising a `finetune` capability the trainer cannot honour, or advertises it with a state that makes the limitation discoverable — an advertised capability that always refuses is a routing lie (the manifest ↔ admission cross-gate rule lugh already enforces).
userStories.notes: Do this even if US-1 stalls. A silent fixture is worse than an honest refusal, and lugh's own design already proves the pattern.

userStories.title: Close the loop with lugh
userStories.description: D9's contract spans two repos; verify it end to end rather than assuming.
acceptanceCriteria: An out-of-envelope job refused by lugh is followed through to agora and the result is recorded — either it trains, or it refuses with a code the caller can act on.
Whatever the outcome, `rosetta/strategy/DECISIONS.md`'s D9 entry is updated so the register does not keep asserting a routing target that behaves differently than described.
Nothing in `~/Development/lugh` is edited by this tasklist — the cross-repo change, if any, is authored there.
userStories.notes: This is the assertion that would have caught the defect: nobody ever followed a refusal across the boundary.
